component.name: SimRig
component.summary: Set up a sim-racing rig of any brand

description.p: SimRig sets up a whole sim-racing rig on Linux: wheel base, steering wheel, pedals, shifter and handbrake, whatever the brand. It installs the drivers the devices need, shows every device moving live, tunes and calibrates them and keeps presets, then steps aside: the devices keep working in every game with SimRig closed.

ul.li: Fanatec, Moza, Logitech, Thrustmaster, PXN, Simagic and standard force feedback bases
Any USB shifter or handbrake, set up by moving it
Drivers installed with one password, kept after kernel updates
Rotation, force feedback and each brand's own settings, saved in the device
What a device cannot do stays visible, with the reason
Checks what games need from each device, and says how to fix it

screenshot.caption: The rig, live: every device drawn as it stands and moving as it is used
A wheel base: rotation, force feedback and its own settings
Pedals: response curve, dead zones and maximum force
A shifter: its gate, gears and reverse

description.p: SimRig shows up in software centres, with its description, screenshots and release notes.

ul.li: Add a device shows the plugin of each device, with Change to pick another one
An unlisted model of a known maker is offered that maker's plugin first
Any device no plugin handles can be given to a plugin by hand
When a plugin does not take a device, the reason shows under its row

description.p: Moza, confirmed on real hardware with an R21 Ultra base, a CS Pro wheel, CRP2 pedals, the HBP handbrake and the SGP shifter.

ul.li: The steering wheel on a Moza base, with its buttons, paddles and settings
Shifters and handbrake plugged into a Moza base show up on their own
The SGP sequential shifter on its own USB, with its extra buttons
Mapping by hand stays available for any device that responds wrong
A USB device no plugin knows can be given to a plugin

description.p: The first release: a whole sim-racing rig set up on Linux, with the drivers its devices need.
